case: Almasri case: investigation of the Prime Minister and three ministers for aiding and abetting and embezzlement (Tribunale dei ministri, Rome)
description: Osama Almasri Njeem, a Libyan judicial-police official wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) for alleged crimes against detainees, was arrested in Turin on 19 January 2025, released on 21 January after the Rome Court of Appeal found the arrest irregular because the Justice Ministry had not acted, and flown back to Libya the same day on an Italian state aircraft. After a complaint by lawyer Luigi Li Gotti, the Rome prosecutor's office registered Meloni, Justice Minister Carlo Nordio, Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi and Undersecretary Alfredo Mantovano as suspects of aiding and abetting (favoreggiamento) and embezzlement (peculato), and transmitted the file to the court for ministerial offences (Tribunale dei ministri), as the law requires. Meloni announced the notice on 28 January 2025.
outcome: On 4 August 2025 Meloni said the Tribunale dei ministri had archived her position, finding no grounds to show that she had an active and decisive role in the decision, while it sought authorisation to proceed against Nordio, Piantedosi and Mantovano. On 9 October 2025 the Chamber of Deputies denied that authorisation in secret ballots, and on 28 October 2025 the Tribunale archived the case against the three for lack of a procedural condition. Meloni was not charged.
court: Collegio per i reati ministeriali (Tribunale dei ministri) at the Rome court; Rome prosecutor's office
presumption_note: Meloni's position was archived (dismissed) at the investigation stage in August 2025; she was never charged or tried and is presumed innocent. The ministers' case was closed after Parliament refused authorisation to proceed, without any finding of guilt.
key_facts: 19–21 January 2025: arrest in Turin, release by the Rome Court of Appeal and repatriation to Libya on an Italian state flight
28 January 2025: Meloni announced she had been notified that she was under investigation
4 August 2025: Tribunale dei ministri archived Meloni's position; Meloni criticised the decision to pursue her ministers but not her
9 October 2025: Chamber denied authorisation to proceed against Nordio, Piantedosi and Mantovano
28 October 2025: case against the three archived

Related, as of October 2026: Nordio's former chief of staff Giusi Bartolozzi faces trial for allegedly giving false information; on 7 July 2026 the Constitutional Court declared admissible the Chamber's conflict-of-powers claim in her case
Related: the ICC found Italy in non-compliance and in a decision made public on 2 April 2026 referred it to the Assembly of States Parties
June 2026: Almasri was sentenced in Libya to 7 years and 4 months for violence against migrants (Il Post)

case: Communication to the ICC Prosecutor alleging complicity in genocide in Gaza (Meloni named with ministers and Leonardo's CEO)
description: A group of jurists and lawyers ('Giuristi e avvocati per la Palestina') sent the ICC Prosecutor a communication under Article 15 of the Rome Statute alleging that Meloni, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, Defence Minister Guido Crosetto and Leonardo CEO Roberto Cingolani were complicit in genocide and other crimes in Gaza through supplies of arms and components to Israel. Meloni herself disclosed the complaint on Rai 1 on 7 October 2025. Such communications can be filed by anyone and do not by themselves open an investigation.
outcome: As of October 2026 no decision by the ICC Prosecutor to open a preliminary examination or investigation concerning Meloni has been reported; an ICC spokesperson told Pagella Politica that only the Prosecutor's decisions have official value.
court: International Criminal Court (Office of the Prosecutor), The Hague
presumption_note: This is a private communication, not a charge or an investigation; no ICC organ has made any finding against Meloni, who is presumed innocent.
key_facts: 7 October 2025: Meloni revealed on 'Porta a Porta' that she had been reported to the ICC
The communication also names Tajani, Crosetto and Cingolani
Reported filing dates differ between sources (early to mid-October 2025)
No ICC investigation of Meloni reported as of October 2026

case: Defamation case against writer Roberto Saviano (Meloni as complainant)
type: criminal defamation (Meloni as complainant / injured party)
description: Meloni, then an opposition leader, filed a defamation complaint after Roberto Saviano, speaking on La7's 'Piazzapulita' in December 2020 about the death of a migrant child crossing the Mediterranean and the rhetoric used against NGOs, said 'bastardi' of her and Matteo Salvini. Salvini joined the proceedings as a civil party. The case drew attention as one brought by a politician who became Prime Minister while it was pending.
outcome: On 12 October 2023 the Rome court found Saviano guilty and imposed a suspended fine of 1,000 euros (prosecutors had requested 10,000), granting mitigating circumstances for having acted for reasons of particular moral value. His lawyer announced an appeal; the outcome of any appeal could not be confirmed as of October 2026.
presumption_note: Meloni is the complainant, not a defendant. The first-instance judgment against Saviano is not final while an appeal is possible, and he is presumed innocent until a final judgment.
key_facts: Remark made on 'Piazzapulita' (La7) in December 2020
12 October 2023: first-instance conviction, suspended €1,000 fine
Appeal announced by the defence; status not confirmed

case: Defamation case against historian Luciano Canfora (Meloni as complainant)
type: criminal defamation (Meloni as complainant / injured party)
description: Meloni filed a complaint, seeking 20,000 euros in damages, after the historian Luciano Canfora, at a conference in a Bari high school in April 2022, described her as 'neonazista nell'animo' ('neo-Nazi at heart') over her stance on the war in Ukraine. Canfora was charged with aggravated defamation and tried in Bari.
outcome: Meloni withdrew the complaint a few days before the hearing, and on 7 October 2024 the Bari court ruled that there were no grounds to proceed (non luogo a procedere), without a verdict on the merits.
presumption_note: Meloni was the complainant. The case ended with no verdict after the complaint was withdrawn; Canfora was not convicted and is presumed innocent.
key_facts: Remark made in April 2022 at a high-school conference in Bari
Meloni sought €20,000 in damages
Complaint withdrawn by Meloni; proceedings closed on 7 October 2024

case: Defamation case against journalist Giulia Cortese (Meloni as complainant)
type: criminal defamation (Meloni as complainant / injured party)
description: Meloni filed a complaint over three posts published on Twitter (now X) on 12 October 2021 by journalist Giulia Cortese: a doctored photo showing Meloni with a picture of Benito Mussolini behind her, and two later posts calling her 'donnetta' and mocking her height ('you are only 1.20 metres tall').
outcome: In July 2024 a Milan court acquitted Cortese over the photomontage post ('il fatto non costituisce reato') and convicted her over the two other posts, imposing a suspended fine of 1,200 euros and 5,000 euros in damages to Meloni. Whether an appeal was filed could not be confirmed.
presumption_note: Meloni is the complainant, not a defendant. The first-instance judgment against Cortese is not final while an appeal is possible, and she is presumed innocent until a final judgment.
key_facts: Posts published on 12 October 2021, when Meloni was in opposition
July 2024: acquittal on one post, conviction on two; suspended €1,200 fine and €5,000 damages
Appeal status not confirmed

case: Deepfake pornographic videos case in Sassari (Meloni as injured party and civil claimant)
type: criminal defamation (Meloni as injured party / civil party)
description: Two private individuals from Sassari are charged with defamation for allegedly superimposing Meloni's face onto pornographic videos that were posted on a US-based website in 2020, before she became Prime Minister, and remained online for months. Meloni joined the proceedings as a civil party seeking 100,000 euros in damages, which she said would go to charity, and was summoned to testify as injured party in July 2024.
outcome: No verdict had been reported in the sources consulted as of October 2026.
presumption_note: Meloni is the injured party, not a defendant. The accused have not been convicted and are presumed innocent; their names are omitted here as they are private individuals.
key_facts: Videos allegedly posted online in 2020
Meloni seeks €100,000 in damages, to be donated to charity
Meloni summoned as a witness/injured party for July 2024 (ANSA)
